As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing site and hosted control panel but no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or other machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Poste Italiane
providers.description: Poste Italiane (Gruppo Poste Italiane S.p.A.) is Italy's national postal operator and largest integrated omnichannel services platform, active in logistics, mail and parcels, financial services (BancoPosta), insurance (Poste Vita, Poste Assicura), payments and telecommunications. Its parcel carrier API for Poste Delivery Business (Delivery Express) is available only to contracted business customers via the MyPDB portal; no public developer documentation or machine-readable contract is published. Surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (market-gap:shipping-logistics).

providers.name: Scania
providers.description: Scania AB is a leading global manufacturer of heavy trucks, buses, and engines, providing sustainable transport solutions and services. Founded in 1891 in Sweden, Scania designs, manufactures, and sells a full range of trucks and buses, as well as engines for marine and industrial applications. The company focuses on innovation, safety, and environmental responsibility, offering digital services and connectivity solutions for fleet management and logistics. Scania operates worldwide, delivering high-quality vehicles and services to customers across various industries, supporting efficient and eco-friendly transportation.

providers.name: StarShip
providers.description: StarShip is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: new-submission) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: Aante
providers.description: Aante (爱安特) is a Chinese factory-automation (FA) parts distributor and one-stop industrial e-commerce procurement platform, operated by Aante (Changzhou) Precision Machinery Co., Ltd. (爱安特（常州）精密机械有限公司) and headquartered in Changzhou, Jiangsu. Established in 2002 as the successor to Sandi Automation, it sells linear motion, transmission, standard, machined, framing, motion-unit, electrical and pneumatic components across 96 product categories and roughly two million SKUs, distributing 30+ international brands including SMC and THK alongside its own Aante-branded line. It serves customers in semiconductors, new energy, 3C electronics, photovoltaics, LCD, automotive, medical and food manufacturing from three production bases and 30+ service centers, and in 2026 acquired software firm Zhuiguang Geometry to pair components with design software. The storefront at ant-fa.com is a Chinese-language Nuxt commerce site; no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract is published.

providers.name: Abacus (Swiss ERP)
providers.description: Abacus (Swiss ERP) provides comprehensive business software solutions for Swiss enterprises, covering financial accounting, payroll, human resources, procurement, and production planning. The platform integrates electronic banking, expense management, and analytics, offering cloud‑based ERP tools tailored to the regulatory and multilingual environment of Switzerland.

providers.name: Backlotcars
providers.description: BacklotCars, Inc. is a dealer-to-dealer wholesale used-vehicle marketplace, founded in Kansas City and acquired by KAR Global (now OPENLANE, Inc.), whose technology was consolidated into the OPENLANE US marketplace. It connects thousands of franchise and independent dealers through a 24/7 bid-ask marketplace, "Buy It Now" listings, and timed auctions scheduled throughout each week, backed by native mobile apps, in-lane vehicle inspections with AI-analyzed engine recordings, transportation, and floor-plan financing. Commercial sellers and dealer groups can push inventory straight from their own systems into OPENLANE Sell via OPENLANE Connect, a lightweight dealer integration API with a dedicated test environment. This profile began as a 500 Global portfolio lead surfaced into the API Evangelist network and was enriched from OPENLANE's public marketing and product surface; the platform publishes no public OpenAPI or open developer portal.

providers.name: Buncha
providers.description: Buncha is a scheduled neighborhood grocery delivery service operating across Minnesota and Michigan. Customers shop online from local partner retailers and receive their orders on set weekly routes, with a single refrigerated van consolidating multiple neighbors' orders into one trip for a $3.45 flat delivery fee. Professional personal shoppers hand-pick items into insulated bags, and the aggregated-route model is positioned to cut delivery CO2 emissions by up to 80% versus on-demand services. Buncha is offered through iOS and Android consumer apps and is backed by Foundry Group and Techstars. It is currently a consumer product with no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Mubit
providers.description: Mubit is a temporary storage and logistics service based in Guadalajara, Mexico, offering on-demand collection, climate-controlled warehousing, digital photo inventory, and delivery for both individuals and businesses. Customers pay only for the space they use, with free pickup and drop-off, optional professional packing, and 24/7 CCTV-monitored facilities across three warehouses (Colli, Tijera, and Casuarina). Backed by 500 Global and Techstars, the company reports 4,000+ customers and a 4.9-star Google rating, and operates a mobile/web customer portal at clientes.mubit.co for scheduling pickups and deliveries and viewing stored items. Mubit publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Portex
providers.description: Portex is a freight procurement and management platform that replaces the emails, spreadsheets, and PDFs of traditional freight quoting with a single collaborative workspace. Shippers, brokers, carriers, and forwarders use Portex to create, send, receive, compare, and award freight quotes up to 90% faster, centralize shipment documents and tracking, chat with carriers, and analyze freight spend for cost-saving recommendations. Founded by Brittany Ennix (previously Uber and Flexport) and backed by Cowboy Ventures, Portex is a seed-stage logistics technology company. As of this profile the platform is delivered as a hosted web application at portexpro.com and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Reframe
providers.description: Reframe (usereframe.ai) is a San Francisco-based Y Combinator Winter 2026 company, founded in 2025 by Bryan Zin (previously a Product Design Engineer on the iPhone team at Apple) and Eric Wiener, building an AI-native hardware procurement platform. Reframe automates the manual procurement process in hardware supply chains: instead of emails and spreadsheets, AI agents handle purchase orders, supplier follow-ups, and part tracking for both COTS and custom-manufactured components, with Slack and Gmail integrations for team workflows. This API Evangelist profile tracks Reframe as a company in the network; the company does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Sanctuary AI
providers.description: Sanctuary AI is a Vancouver, British Columbia humanoid robotics company on a mission to create and deploy industrial-grade general-purpose humanoid robots to help address growing labor challenges. Its flagship product is Phoenix, a bipedal humanoid robot designed for dull, dirty, and dangerous work in automotive, manufacturing, and logistics environments. Phoenix is driven by Carbon, Sanctuary AI's proprietary AI control system that mimics human cognitive subsystems — memory, sight, sound, and touch — to translate natural-language tasks into dexterous physical actions. The company is vertically integrated, designing everything from motors and actuators through to generative AI algorithms in-house. Co-founded by James Wells (CEO) and Olivia Norton (CTO/CPO), Sanctuary AI has a private GitHub organization with no public repositories, no developer portal, no public API, no SDK, and no published OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specifications. The commercial model is hardware sales and enterprise deployments; Carbon is a proprietary on-board system and there is no public developer surface.

providers.name: SeeChange
providers.description: SeeChange Technologies provides retail loss prevention software powered by computer vision AI. Their platform optimizes inventory management, enhances customer insights, and elevates in‑store experiences by detecting shoplifting, out‑of‑stock items, and shopper behavior in real time. The solution helps retailers reduce shrinkage, improve operational efficiency, and deliver smarter, safer, and connected environments across stores.

providers.name: Silq
providers.description: Silq (OneSilq) is a digital freight forwarder delivering fast, transparent global shipping and supply-chain services. Offerings span ocean freight (full container load, less-than-container load and shared container load), air freight, buyer's consolidation, cargo value protection, customs brokerage and trucking/drayage, plus quality-control inspections across China, India, Vietnam, Indonesia and Bangladesh. The platform layers real-time shipment visibility, live ocean-carrier freight rates, expert trade advisory and built-in risk protection for importers and small shippers.

providers.name: Verve Motion
providers.description: Verve Motion is a wearable robotics company spun out of the Harvard Biodesign Lab that builds SafeLift, a soft powered exosuit for industrial workers who lift repetitively. Inertial sensors woven into the suit detect lifting motion and trigger assistive force that the company says takes up to 40% of the strain off a worker's back, while Verve Logic — its cloud platform — collects the resulting movement data and reports ergonomic risk, unsafe-posture trends and exosuit utilization to safety managers. SafeLift is sold as a subscription bundling the exosuit, the Verve Logic data portal and Verve Care support, and is distributed in part through partners such as HexArmor. Verve Motion publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the Verve Logic portal at logic.vervemotion.com is a customer-only single-page application that disallows crawling in robots.txt.

providers.name: Metcash
providers.description: Metcash Limited is Australia's leading wholesale distribution and marketing company, with a diversified business across food, grocery, hardware and liquor. It supplies and supports independent retailers under banners including IGA, Foodland, Campbells, Superior Food, Mitre 10, Home Hardware, Total Tools, Hardings Hardware, Cellarbrations, IGA Liquor and the Bottle-O, and operates the MetConnect retailer portal. Metcash is listed on the ASX. It was surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (australia-apidays-2026); no public developer API or documentation was identified on metcash.com.

providers.name: Packhelp
providers.description: Packhelp is a European custom and wholesale packaging platform that lets businesses design, order, and warehouse branded packaging — boxes, mailers, bags, tubes, and accessories — through online design tools and a curated catalog of EU-based producers. Packhelp also markets "the first-ever API for packaging," a sales-gated set of web services that let 3PL, fulfillment, marketplace, logistics, and food-delivery platforms embed packaging quoting, ordering, and a drag-and-drop packaging editor directly into their own applications and whitelabel storefronts.

providers.name: Pallet
providers.description: Pallet builds an AI-powered logistics workforce: autonomous AI agents that automate supply chain operations for freight brokerages, freight forwarders, FTL and LTL carriers, warehouses, and shippers. Its agents handle end-to-end workflows from quoting through order entry, track-and-trace, billing, and customer service, integrating with existing TMS, WMS, email, and legacy applications. The Atlas product surfaces revenue opportunities across freight operations. Pallet is backed by Bain Capital Ventures and General Catalyst. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Papaya
providers.description: Papayadash provides AI‑powered fleet intelligence software that helps fleet operators streamline data collection, reduce total cost of ownership, maximize vehicle uptime, and accelerate the transition to sustainable, electric fleets. The platform offers real‑time analytics, predictive maintenance, and a unified data layer for fleet management across diverse vehicle types.

providers.name: Auger
providers.description: Auger provides an operating system for supply chain finance, ingesting raw operational streams such as ERPs, spreadsheets, and legacy APIs to unlock trapped working capital. The platform automates coordination, reduces lead times, and offers AI‑driven insights to help enterprises accelerate execution and capture billions of dollars in value.

providers.name: Trackonomy
providers.description: Trackonomy is a supply chain visibility company that digitizes real-world operations with barely-there smart label sensors. Its SmartTape and THL Tape products provide item-level tracking, monitoring location, temperature, humidity, and light in real time, while its platform connects, automates, controls, and remediates operations processes at global scale for logistics, industrial, utilities, healthcare, government, and airline customers. Trackonomy is backed by 8VC. It advertises a customizable RESTful API and webhook-based real-time data exchange for platform customers, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Cloverpop
providers.description: Cloverpop provides an Enterprise Decision Intelligence Platform that combines AI, human expertise, and business processes to accelerate and improve decision-making across organizations. Their solutions include Decision Intelligence Platform, CloverPlan Forecasting, D‑Sight™, and Decision‑Back™ Transformation, helping enterprises achieve faster decisions, higher ROI, and resilient operations.

providers.name: Djust
providers.description: DJUST is a French all-in-one, modular B2B commerce platform that helps distributors, wholesalers, manufacturers and retailers launch and automate their B2B eCommerce and eProcurement operations. The platform covers automated order management (24/7 online ordering), AI-assisted quoting with automatic pricing and discounts, integrated online payments with deadline tracking, a conversational AI sales assistant, real-time sales analytics, and prebuilt ERP/CRM integrations. Customers include Eiffage, Auchan Retail and Lesaffre; DJUST reports EUR 1.5B GMV and 2M orders processed in 2025. Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Olist
providers.description: Olist is a Brazilian commerce technology company headquartered in Curitiba, Paraná, offering an integrated ecosystem of solutions that automate business management for online sellers. Its products include an ERP for inventory, invoicing and order automation, a multi-marketplace Integration Hub (Mercado Livre, TikTok Shop and others), a POS for physical stores, a digital account with Pix payments, shipping and fulfillment (Envios), and storefront creation. Olist exposes robust partner APIs through its Technology Partner program ("Parceiro Tecnológico"), where approved developers receive test credentials and Swagger documentation to build and homologate integrations reaching 60,000+ merchants. The public API surface is gated behind partner registration; no open developer portal or OpenAPI specification is published.

providers.name: Fleetmatics
providers.description: Fleetmatics was a fleet management, telematics, and GPS vehicle tracking SaaS company whose Reveal platform tracked commercial vehicles, drivers, and mobile assets for small and mid-sized fleets. Founded in Dublin and later headquartered in Massachusetts, Fleetmatics IPO'd on the NYSE in 2012 and was acquired by Verizon in 2016 for about USD 2.4 billion, becoming the core of Verizon Connect. Its Reveal platform exposes a documented REST API and webhook suite - the Fleetmatics Integration Manager (FIM) / Reveal Integration Services APIs - covering vehicles, drivers, GPS positions and history, trips and segments, driver status and safety, hours-of-service logbooks, geofences (places), groups, and non-powered asset tracking. The API gateway still runs on Fleetmatics-branded hosts (fim.api.us.fleetmatics.com); access is gated to Reveal customers and approved integration partners who request Integration Manager and Reveal REST credentials before calling the documented endpoints. The Fleetmatics brand now redirects to Verizon Connect.

providers.name: Geocento Limited
providers.description: Geocento Limited provides end‑to‑end virtual constellation design, procurement and management services for earth observation data. Leveraging extensive consulting expertise, they help organisations build and operate custom satellite imaging constellations, offering consultancy, technology platforms, and full‑service procurement to enhance sovereign capabilities and programmatic resilience.

providers.name: American Axle and Manufacturing
providers.description: American Axle & Manufacturing (AAM), now operating as Dauch Corporation following the February 2026 acquisition of Dowlais Group (GKN Automotive and GKN Powder Metallurgy), is a global Tier 1 automotive supplier designing, engineering, and manufacturing driveline and metal forming technologies for electric, hybrid, and internal combustion vehicles. AAM operates an iSupplier Portal for supplier communication, EDI integration for forecasts and releases, and the Demand AAM aftermarket parts portal.

providers.name: Another
providers.description: Another is an AI-native software platform that modernizes off-channel and off-price inventory operations for fashion, beauty, and retail brands. Founded in 2024 by Corina Marshall, the platform connects to a retailer's existing systems - including returns management - to create a single source of truth for excess, returned, and pre-loved goods, then automates how brands identify, manage, and monetize that inventory across downstream channels. Teams can invite and connect with secondary merchandise recipients, send inventory proposals to buyers, request payment from partners, and let partners request inventory, replacing fragmented manual workflows spread across teams, buyers, channels, and partners. Another closed a $2.5M seed round in January 2026 co-led by Anthemis and Westbound. As of this profile the company operates a private, invite-based web application and publishes no public API, developer portal, or technical documentation.

providers.name: Berkshire Grey
providers.description: Berkshire Grey is a Bedford, Massachusetts-based AI and robotics company that builds integrated pick-and-place, parcel sortation, trailer-unloading, and shuttle-sortation systems for eCommerce fulfillment, retail replenishment, and parcel logistics operations. Its product portfolio is organized around four flagship robotic systems — Core robotic picking system, Dispatch parcel sorter, Scoop trailer unloader, and Stride shuttle sorter — supported by the BG Flex mobile robotic platform and a centralized operating environment that orchestrates fleets of industrial-grade mobile robots for induct, transport, sort, sequence, and fulfill workflows including buy-online-pickup-in-store, curbside, and store replenishment. The company holds 700+ awarded patents (300+ pending) and has deployed solutions with Global-100 retailers and logistics service providers including Walmart, Target, and FedEx, with FedEx expanding from small-parcel sortation into broader AI robotic package-handling capabilities. Berkshire Grey originally went public via SPAC merger with Revolution Acceleration Acquisition Corp in 2021, then entered into a definitive merger agreement with SoftBank Group in 2023 (approximately $375M / $1.40 per share) and is now operated as a private SoftBank portfolio company. Integration with warehouse-management systems is delivered through a proprietary RESTful API surfaced via professional services and a 24/7 remote monitoring and predictive-maintenance support model; the API, BG-OS platform, and any associated SDKs are not publicly documented, and Berkshire Grey does not operate a public developer portal, downloadable SDK, or open-source release for its robotic operating environment.

providers.name: CDW
providers.description: CDW is a leading multi-brand provider of information technology solutions to business, government, education, and healthcare customers. CDW offers eProcurement integration capabilities including a Catalog API, PunchOut (cXML/OCI), electronic purchase ordering, and electronic invoicing to enable procurement system integration with partners such as SAP Ariba, Coupa, Oracle, and Jaggaer.

providers.name: Fleetline
providers.description: Fleetline is an all-in-one AI dispatch and fleet-optimization platform for trucking fleets. Its AI-based dispatch engine ingests load, driver, and ELD data, simulates billions of scenarios, and recommends the best assignment plan so operators maximize revenue, productivity, and fleet utilization. The platform aggregates major load boards into a unified workspace, identifies schedule gaps and fills them with spot loads, composes complex trips with tradeoff analysis, forecasts delays, breakdowns, and HOS violations, and includes an AI assistant trained on fleet history and TMS data. Fleetline is a Bloomberg Beta portfolio company; it exposes a marketing site, a customer login/auth portal, and an internal API host, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Normative
providers.description: Normative is a Stockholm, Sweden-based carbon accounting and ESG reporting software company helping enterprises measure, report, and reduce their greenhouse gas emissions across scopes 1, 2, and 3. Its platform combines a library of more than 349,000 region- and sector-specific emission factors with workflows for product carbon footprint (PCF), supply chain engagement, Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) target setting, Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) disclosure, and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) reporting. Calculations are built to the GHG Protocol and independently verified by TÜV SÜD against ISO/IEC 25051. Customers include Vodafone, Hertz, Hitachi Rail, and Flying Tiger Copenhagen, and every account is paired with a named, GHG Protocol-certified Climate Strategy Advisor rather than a traditional support helpdesk. The company's revenue model is enterprise SaaS subscriptions plus advisory services; Normative does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or open-source release, and its GitHub organization (normative-io) currently exposes no public repositories.

providers.name: Reindeer AI
providers.description: Reindeer AI is an enterprise agentic AI platform that automates back-office business operations across finance, banking, insurance, supply chain, procurement, legal compliance, and global business services. Founded in 2024 with offices in New York and Tel Aviv, Reindeer deploys custom AI agents that learn from operational workflows using its Fast Track Training approach (functional models in roughly two weeks from a small number of samples), with human-in-the-loop escalation, continuous learning, and Model Reality Grounding safeguards against hallucination. It ships 200+ pre-trained skills and 200+ out-of-the-box integrations into systems such as SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Workday, ServiceNow, and Salesforce, is model-agnostic (Claude, GPT, Gemini, Bedrock, DeepSeek, GLM), and emphasizes customer data ownership and enterprise security (ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type 2, GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA). Reindeer is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, TEAM8, and Vesey Ventures. Reindeer does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or a developer portal; the product is delivered as an enterprise engagement, so this profile captures company identity and security posture rather than an API surface.

providers.name: AutoTrac
providers.description: AutoTrac is a Brazilian fleet management and vehicle tracking technology company with over 30 years of experience. As the national market leader, AutoTrac provides satellite and cellular fleet tracking solutions, real-time telemetry, driver journey management, and management intelligence platforms for logistics, agriculture, maritime, and insurance sectors. The company operates its own terrestrial satellite communication station and data center for nationwide coverage.

providers.name: Carpool Logistics
providers.description: Carpool Logistics provides end‑to‑end vehicle logistics with a documented chain of custody, moving over 200,000 vehicles annually for dealers, OEMs, fleets and individuals. Their platform offers managed transport, white‑glove home delivery, auction services, and digital tools like a browser extension and CarPass identity‑verified vehicle release, all accessible via a modern web portal.

providers.name: Convey
providers.description: project44 provides a decision intelligence platform that connects shippers, logistics service providers and carriers to enable real‑time visibility, analytics and automated actions across the supply chain. Its solutions include carrier onboarding, transportation management, yard management, e‑commerce logistics and AI‑driven orchestration for tasks such as rating, booking and exception handling. The platform serves global enterprises in industries such as automotive, retail, manufacturing and food & beverage.

providers.name: Nuvocargo
providers.description: Nuvocargo is an AI-powered freight-management platform for North American truckload logistics, focused on the US-Mexico-Canada cross-border corridor. Its "Nuvo AI" system coordinates a network of specialized agents (quoting, negotiation, booking, dispatch, tracking, exception handling, audit, and payment) to automate the freight load lifecycle, and it pairs that software with licensed freight brokerage, managed transportation, and customs-brokerage services. The company was surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Homebrew and QED Investors. As of this enrichment pass Nuvocargo publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; onboarding is contact-gated ("zero-integration" pilots), so this profile captures the company identity, legal/resource surface, and domain-security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Apeel
providers.description: Apeel (Apeel Sciences) is a food technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Goleta, California. It produces a plant-derived, edible coating, made from lipids and glycerolipids found in the peels, seeds and pulp of produce, that is applied to fresh fruit and vegetables at packing houses to slow water loss and oxidation, extending shelf life and reducing food waste across the supply chain. Apeel-treated produce is sold through grocery retailers in multiple countries. In 2021 Apeel acquired ImpactVision and added hyperspectral imaging to its supplier installations to grade interior quality, ripeness and freshness. Apeel is a materials-science and supply-chain operator: as of this profile it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API contract, or self-serve developer sign-up.

providers.name: Arrive AI
providers.description: Arrive AI (Nasdaq: ARAI) is an autonomous last-mile delivery company headquartered in Fishers, Indiana, founded by Dan O'Toole and originally operating as DroneDek. Its patented Autonomous Last Mile (ALM) platform is anchored by the Arrive Point, an AI-powered smart mailbox that accepts and dispatches parcels to and from drones, ground robots and human couriers, with temperature-controlled compartments, real-time tracking, smart logistics alerts and chain-of-custody controls aimed at healthcare, pharmacy and e-commerce logistics. The company markets hardware plus a network service; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Coco Robotics
providers.description: Coco Robotics is a Santa Monica, California urban robotics company operating a fleet of zero-emission, remotely-supervised sidewalk delivery robots ("Cocobots") for last-mile food, grocery and retail delivery. Merchants do not integrate with Coco directly: Coco is consumed as a delivery service provider through Uber Eats, DoorDash, Wolt and Olo Dispatch, and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or webhooks of its own. Its public software surface is limited to a marketing site, a customer order-tracking web app, and a GitHub organization of forked ROS and infrastructure tooling.

providers.name: Starship Technologies
providers.description: Starship Technologies is an autonomous last-mile delivery company that operates a global fleet of self-driving, sidewalk-going delivery robots. Founded in 2014 by Skype co-founders Ahti Heinla and Janus Friis, the company runs commercial robot delivery on university campuses, in residential neighborhoods, on industrial sites and for grocery and restaurant partners across the United States, the United Kingdom, Estonia, Finland, Germany and Denmark, and has completed more than 10 million autonomous deliveries. Its commercial product, Delivery by Starship, is a delivery-as-a-service offering that partners integrate into their own ordering apps: Starship states that its APIs let a partner create delivery jobs, load robots, obtain status updates and handle delivery cancellations, backed by a developer toolkit, documentation, ready-made components and support. That developer surface is not published to the open web — Starship provides it to partners after a commercial conversation via business@starship.co, so no public specification, reference or portal exists to profile.

providers.name: Anixter International
providers.description: Anixter International was a leading global distributor of network and security solutions, electrical and electronic solutions, and utility power solutions. In June 2020, Anixter was acquired by Wesco International for approximately $4.5 billion, creating a combined company with over $17 billion in annual revenue. Anixter now operates as Wesco Anixter, providing B2B distribution, supply chain services, and digital integration capabilities including EDI, punchout catalogs, and procurement system integrations.

providers.name: Assiduusglobal
providers.description: Assiduusglobal, operating as Assiduus Global, provides a cross‑border e‑commerce acceleration platform that unifies supply‑chain, marketplace, and brand‑protection services. Leveraging AI‑driven consumer insights, the company offers tools such as Brand Central, Ship With Assiduus, and Aacarto to help brands expand globally across 20+ countries, accelerate marketplace listings, and gain real‑time analytics. The platform serves Fortune 500 clients and aims to simplify international growth through data‑rich middleware.

providers.name: Bright Machines
providers.description: Bright Machines is a San Francisco-based software-defined manufacturing company founded in 2018 by Amar Hanspal and Lior Susan that builds a full-stack intelligent automation platform for electronics and AI-infrastructure assembly. Its Microfactory pairs modular Bright Robotic Cells with Brightware, a platform operating system that orchestrates hardware, runs a machine-vision "Smart Skills" perception stack, and provides manufacturing-execution services for work orders, material management and real-time production KPIs. Bright Data, the company's data layer, unifies component, process and enterprise-system data through secure APIs and auditable data flows, and Bright Designer turns product CAD into assembly-ready digital twins using NVIDIA Omniverse on Microsoft Azure. The company has raised roughly $279M from Eclipse, BlackRock, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Jabil and others. All platform and data interfaces are delivered to customers under commercial engagement; Bright Machines publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API contracts.

providers.name: Plus One Robotics
providers.description: Plus One Robotics is a San Antonio, Texas warehouse-automation company founded in 2016 by Erik Nieves and Shaun Edwards that builds AI-powered computer-vision software and robotic work cells for parcel handling, depalletizing, palletizing and induction. Its PickOne perception system tells a robot arm how to grasp each item and verifies placement, while Yonder provides supervised autonomy — remote human "Crew Chiefs" who take over when the robot hits an exception. Packaged work cells DepalOne and InductOne wrap that stack in deployable hardware. The company reports more than 1.5 billion lifetime picks across robots fielded in 15 countries, with additional offices in Eindhoven (Netherlands) and Boulder, Colorado. Plus One Robotics publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; product integration is handled through its partner channel and a login-gated partner portal.

providers.name: SESAMm
providers.description: SESAMm provides AI‑powered ESG and reputational risk intelligence, monitoring controversies and exposure across over 5 million public and private companies. Leveraging more than 30 billion documents, its platform helps organizations assess ESG risks, track reputational issues, and make data‑driven decisions.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: AgriAku
providers.description: AgriAku (PT Agriaku Digital Indonesia) is a Jakarta-based agritech company founded in 2021 that digitizes the distribution of agricultural inputs - seeds, fertilizers, crop protection, nutrients and farm tools - to Indonesia's network of independent farm-supply shops (toko tani). Partner shops order from a catalog of more than 15,000 agricultural products through the AgriAku Mitra Android app, while separate vendor, seller and courier applications cover the rest of the supply chain. The company reports more than 23,390 partners across Indonesia and has raised roughly USD 46M from Alpha JWC Ventures, Go-Ventures and MDI Ventures. AgriAku operates no public developer program: every API host it runs is a private backend for its own first-party mobile and web applications.

providers.name: Clicoh
providers.description: Clicoh provides intelligent logistics solutions for e‑commerce businesses, offering AI‑powered warehousing, fulfillment, and last‑mile delivery across multiple countries. Their platform enables merchants to reduce costs, accelerate sales, and ensure high on‑time delivery rates through integrated storage, custom packaging, and real‑time tracking.

providers.name: Elroy Air
providers.description: Elroy Air develops autonomous vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft for defense, commercial, and rapid-response logistics. Its flagship Chaparral is a hybrid-electric aircraft designed to carry up to 300 pounds of cargo across roughly 300 miles with no crew onboard, taking off and landing vertically and cruising autonomously between points. Founded in 2016 and based in San Francisco, the company works with partners including FedEx, NASA, the U.S. Air Force, and Lockheed Martin, and was selected for the U.S. Department of Transportation eVTOL Integration Pilot Program. Elroy Air is a hardware and autonomy company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or MCP surface. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with identity and domain-security data.

providers.name: Indrive
providers.description: inDrive is a global ride-hailing, delivery, and urban-services platform built around a peer-to-peer, name-your-price model in which passengers propose a fare and nearby drivers accept, counter, or decline it directly. Founded in 2012 by Arsen Tomsky in Yakutsk, Russia and now headquartered in Mountain View, California, the company operates across roughly 48 countries and more than 1,000 cities, with over 400 million app downloads. Beyond city rides it offers intercity transport, courier and freight delivery, on-demand task services, and driver lending. inDrive was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Bond Capital and General Catalyst. inDrive does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal; its GitHub organization hosts internal engineering frameworks and an engineering handbook rather than external API definitions.

providers.name: Sensefinity
providers.description: Sensefinity is a supply-chain IoT company ("The IoT Transformation Company") delivering real-time tracking, monitoring, and analytics for global cargo and logistics operations. Its platform combines GPS/NB-IoT tracking devices for maritime containers, pallets, and vehicles with temperature and condition (cold-chain) sensors, indoor location tracking, a cloud analytics and machine learning layer, and digital product passport / blockchain integrations. The operational platform is delivered as a hosted web application (uiadmin.sensefinity.com) and mobile asset-management apps, serving enterprise customers across food, pharma, automotive, and manufacturing supply chains. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published as of this profile; a private API host (api.sensefinity.com) backs the platform.

providers.name: SpartanNash
providers.description: SpartanNash is a Byron Center, Michigan food solutions company that operates as both a wholesale grocery distributor and a retail grocer. Its wholesale segment supplies roughly 2,100 independent retail locations, national accounts and e-commerce partners from a network of distribution centers, and through its MDV business it is the leading distributor of grocery products to United States military commissaries and exchanges worldwide. Its retail segment operates roughly 200 corporate-owned supermarkets under banners including Family Fare, Martin's Super Markets, D&W Fresh Market, VG's Grocery, Dan's Supermarket, Family Fresh Market, Needler's Fresh Market, Fresh City Market, Forest Hills Foods and Supermercado Nuestra Familia, alongside pharmacy and fuel centers. Formed by the 2013 merger of Spartan Stores and Nash Finch, the company traded on Nasdaq as SPTN until C&S Wholesale Grocers completed its acquisition of SpartanNash on September 22, 2025; SpartanNash now operates as part of C&S and its corporate web properties are progressively being folded into cswg.com. SpartanNash publishes no public developer program, API documentation or machine-readable API contract; supplier and customer system integration is transacted over EDI through trading-partner onboarding rather than a public API.

providers.name: Stockly
providers.description: Stockly (Stockly SAS, headquartered in Vitry-sur-Seine, France) operates a global inventory network for e-commerce, positioning itself as "the first global inventory for Retail." It connects online retailers that are missing stock (Demanders) with brands and official retailers that hold surplus inventory (Suppliers), detecting out-of-stock variants and filling the gaps in real time so that e-shops never run out of stock. Stockly integrates directly with a retailer's e-commerce infrastructure via API, a CMS, or a marketplace, and is building toward a stock exchange for e-commerce inventory in compliance with brands' distribution policies. The company reports 300+ partnered retailers across Europe and 100M+ available items, and is backed by Techstars. Stockly is primarily a partner-onboarded platform rather than a broad self-serve public developer API.

providers.name: Stuf Storage
providers.description: Stuf is a next-generation, tech-enabled self-storage operator that partners with commercial real estate owners to convert underutilized space — basements, garages and retail vacancies — into modern neighborhood storage facilities. Stuf runs 36 facilities across seven US metros (New York City, Los Angeles, the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, Atlanta, Boston and Washington, DC). Members search and book units online, pay month-to-month with all-inclusive pricing and no hidden fees, and open facility doors with a digital key issued through the Stuf Member Dashboard. Stuf publishes no public developer program, API, or machine-readable API contract; the one machine-readable surface it does serve is a substantial, actively maintained llms.txt at https://www.stufstorage.com/llms.txt, alongside an AI-crawler-permissive robots.txt.

providers.name: Udaan
providers.description: Udaan is India's largest eB2B trade platform, connecting small businesses - kirana stores, chemists, hotels, restaurants, and offices - with manufacturers, brands, and wholesalers across categories including FMCG, staples, fruits and vegetables, pharma, and general merchandise. The platform combines supply chain and logistics operations with financial services for small businesses through udaanCapital, its working-capital fintech arm. Udaan is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and GGV Capital. It publishes no public developer API; buyer and seller experiences are delivered through its web and mobile apps, with api.udaan.com serving as the private app backend.

providers.name: Datakrew
providers.description: Datakrew is a Singapore-based deep-tech company, a spin-off from NTU Singapore supported by Enterprise Singapore, building EV battery intelligence, fleet management, and AI-driven telematics for logistics and delivery, public transport, vehicle OEMs, rental/leasing and shared mobility operators, and mining and construction fleets. Its integrated hardware, software, and AI stack spans the OxRed (MyFleet) fleet-management and intelligence platform, OxRed Lens camera-based visualization telematics, OxRed AutoCert automated certification and compliance, GuardianAI driver-safety and collision-warning analytics, the Ask OX natural-language fleet assistant, and the ITUS Max and ITUS AutoScan edge terminals for telemetry, CAN-bus integration, and vehicle diagnostics, all aimed at optimizing battery health, safety, and operational efficiency.

providers.name: Kodiak AI
providers.description: Kodiak AI, Inc. (formerly Kodiak Robotics) is a Mountain View, California company building the Kodiak Driver, an AI-powered ground autonomy system for driverless trucking and defense vehicles. Founded in April 2018 by Don Burnette, Kodiak develops a purpose-built autonomous driving stack — sensor pods, 4D radar, sparse maps, and fallback systems — that integrates into third-party driving platforms rather than shipping a vehicle of its own. The company runs commercial driverless freight lanes in Texas, Oklahoma, Ohio and Indiana with partners including Atlas Energy Solutions, Maersk, Martin Brower, Roehl Transport, JB Hunt and Werner, and it adapts the same driver to defense and industrial missions with General Dynamics Land Systems, Textron Systems and the US Army. Kodiak raised a $125M Series B in 2021 with Lightspeed Venture Partners, Battery Ventures, CRV, SIP Global Partners and others participating, and became a public company through a business combination with Ares Acquisition Corporation II. Kodiak publishes a corporate web presence, a news/RSS feed and an llms.txt for agents, but does not currently operate a public developer program, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Seaboard
providers.description: Seaboard Corporation is a diversified global agribusiness and transportation holding company headquartered in Merriam, Kansas, operating through Seaboard Foods (pork production and processing), Seaboard Marine (containerized ocean cargo between the United States, the Caribbean, and Central and South America), Seaboard Overseas and Trading Group (grain merchandising and milling), Seaboard Energy (renewable diesel), Transcontinental Capital Corporation (electric power generation in the Dominican Republic), Mount Dora Farms, and a minority interest in Butterball. Seaboard publishes no public developer API or developer portal; its only documented machine-to-machine integration surface is the Seaboard Marine Electronic Data Interchange program, which publishes an ANSI ASC X12 and UN/EDIFACT transaction-set catalog and onboards trading partners through a request form.

providers.name: Cargolux
providers.description: Cargolux Airlines International S.A. is Europe's largest all-cargo airline, headquartered at Luxembourg Findel Airport in Luxembourg and operating a global Boeing 747 freighter network under IATA designator CV and air waybill prefix 172 (with Cargolux Italia on prefix 356). In the logistics chain Cargolux is the main-leg air carrier: it sells capacity to freight forwarders and general sales agents rather than to shippers, hands cargo to terminal and ground handling operators such as its Luxcargo Handling subsidiary, and files customs and security data on behalf of the contracted forwarder. Its API posture is honestly a customer-contract one. Cargolux publishes no developer portal and no machine-readable contract of any kind — developer.cargolux.com, developers.cargolux.com and docs.cargolux.com do not resolve, and /developers, /api, /openapi.json, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /.well-known/ all return 404 on www.cargolux.com. The only public self-service surfaces are HTML: a track-and-trace widget and a flight scheduler on the marketing site, plus a login-walled Customer Portal at my.cargolux.com. A real quote-and- booking API exists, but it is a bilateral, commercially negotiated forwarder interface — piloted with Kuehne+Nagel in 2021 and extended to DB Schenker — with no published reference, and it is complemented by indirect distribution through the cargo.one, CargoAi and WebCargo by Freightos marketplaces. Underneath, Cargolux runs IBS Software's iCargo SaaS cargo management system and holds a large minority stake in Luxembourg's CHAMP Cargosystems, whose developer.champ.aero portal is the developer surface Cargolux's ecosystem actually reads — CHAMP's, not Cargolux's. IATA e-AWB "Single Process" is documented; no IATA ONE Record or Cargo-XML publication was found.

providers.name: Delek US Holdings
providers.description: Delek US Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: DK) is a diversified downstream energy company headquartered in Brentwood, Tennessee with assets in petroleum refining, logistics, asphalt operations, renewable fuels, and convenience store retailing. Delek operates four refineries in Tyler and Big Spring (Texas), El Dorado (Arkansas), and Krotz Springs (Louisiana) with combined crude throughput capacity of roughly 302,000 barrels per day. Logistics assets are operated through Delek Logistics Partners (NYSE: DKL). The company provides investor relations and ESG reporting on its public website but does not publish a developer API; partner integrations occur through industry-standard EDI, terminal automation, and ticketing systems.

providers.name: Logility
providers.description: Logility is an AI-powered supply chain planning platform providing solutions for demand sensing, inventory optimization, supply planning, S&OP process management, and supply chain analytics. Part of Aptean, Logility serves 600+ clients across 80 countries with capabilities for demand planning, inventory optimization, scenario planning, manufacturing execution, and supplier management across 12+ industry verticals.

providers.name: Streamlane
providers.description: Streamlane provides an agentic parcel spend management platform for modern operators, helping retailers and 3PLs unify shipping data, automate invoice audits, and optimize network decisions. Their solution reduces parcel spend by 15‑20% through rate benchmarking, network modeling, and contract negotiation insights.

providers.name: TJX Companies
providers.description: The TJX Companies, Inc. is an American multinational off-price department store corporation headquartered in Framingham, Massachusetts, ranked No. 80 on the 2024 Fortune 500 list. Operating over 4,800 stores across nine countries and three continents under brands including T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods, Sierra, HomeSense (US), and Winners, HomeSense, Marshalls (Canada), TJX provides supplier and vendor integration through EDI and web-based portal platforms. Supplier connectivity is handled via Oracle iSupplier, SupplierOne, and the DiCentral ASN Vendor Portal, supporting purchase orders, advanced shipping notices, invoicing, and payment tracking.

providers.name: Antheia
providers.description: Antheia, Inc. is a Menlo Park, California synthetic-biology company that manufactures biosynthetic key starting materials (KSMs) and active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) for essential medicines. Founded on Christina Smolke's Stanford research, Antheia engineers yeast strains that reconstruct long, complex plant biosynthetic pathways and ferment sugar into molecules previously obtainable only through agricultural cultivation, compressing production timelines from years to weeks. Commercial products include fermentation-derived thebaine, oripavine and scopolamine, with a development pipeline of 70+ KSMs and APIs spanning neurology, gastrointestinal and oncology programs. NOTE FOR THE CATALOG: Antheia's "APIs" are Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, not web APIs — the company publishes no developer API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: AptDeco
providers.description: AptDeco is a full-service online marketplace for buying and selling used, new, and vintage furniture. Founded in 2014 in New York City by Reham Fagiri and Kalam Dennis, the company handles the entire resale transaction end to end: pickup, disassembly and assembly, delivery, payment, scheduling, and logistics are all carried out by its own trained delivery teams. AptDeco serves the New York City metro, New Jersey, Connecticut, Philadelphia, Delaware, and the San Francisco Bay Area, and has expanded to additional US metros with national shipping. Backed by Y Combinator and Initialized Capital. AptDeco does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, legal, and developer surfaces for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Faire
providers.description: Faire is a wholesale marketplace connecting independent retailers with brands. The Faire External API v2 supports both sides of the marketplace: brand-side endpoints for products, orders, inventory, and shipments, and retailer-side endpoints for browsing and ordering.

providers.name: sherpa
providers.description: sherpa is an AI operating system for External Workforce Management (EWM) that runs an enterprise's contingent-labor program end to end with autonomous agents, replacing the work traditionally done by a VMS (Vendor Management System) and MSP (Managed Service Provider). Its agents cover every phase of an external engagement: autonomous intake and classification from Slack, email, Teams or voice; collaborative scope, role and budget drafting; autonomous sourcing with market-benchmarked rates and ranked candidates and suppliers; coordinated screening interviews scored against a weighted rubric; autonomous hiring and onboarding (documents, background and compliance checks, contracts, provisioning, hardware and badges); and active management and payment with a dedicated PM agent, live spend visibility and flexible payouts once outcomes are verified. One platform spans every worker type — contingent labor, freelancers / independent contractors (with a built-in Agent of Record), SOW / services engagements, and, coming soon, AI agents as a managed worker type — with rate intelligence, compliance management and analytics built in. sherpa launched out of stealth with a $2.2M pre-seed round and is backed by Seedcamp and Y Combinator.

providers.name: Autoxing
providers.description: AutoXing is a leading provider of intelligent robot services based on autonomous driving technology. The company focuses on AGV and AMR robots for factories, logistics, restaurants, and hotels, aiming to empower smart retail and improve efficiency through AI-driven navigation and big data integration. AutoXing’s mission is to use smart technology to enable a better life, offering a range of autonomous delivery vehicles, robot chassis, and customized solutions for various industries.

providers.name: Battery Smart
providers.description: Battery Smart is India's largest battery-swapping network for electric two- and three-wheelers, founded in 2019 by Pulkit Khurana and Siddharth Sikka and operated from New Delhi by Upgrid Solutions Private Limited and Upgrid Electrilease Private Limited. It runs an asset-light, partner-led model: local businesses — kirana stores, petrol pumps and neighbourhood shops — host swap points where a driver exchanges a depleted lithium-ion pack for a charged one in roughly two minutes and pays per swap instead of buying the battery with the vehicle, which removes the single largest cost from an electric two- or three-wheeler. The network is concentrated in Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Jaipur and Lucknow, and the company has raised across eleven rounds including a USD 65 million Series B led by LeapFrog Investments with MUFG Bank, Panasonic, Ecosystem Integrity Fund, Blume Ventures and British International Investment participating, plus a USD 15 million debt round with Mirova in April 2026. Battery Smart's software ships only as end-user Android applications — Battery Smart Driver and Battery Smart Partner — backed by a production API host at api.upgrid.in that self-identifies as the "Battery Smart API". As of this profile the company publishes no developer portal, API reference, SDK, webhook catalog or machine-readable specification of any kind.

providers.name: Cycle
providers.description: CYCLE (operated by CM Invest B.V., Amsterdam) is a European electric-mobility subscription service that provides e-bikes and cargo bikes to professional delivery riders, couriers, and businesses. Its all-inclusive monthly subscriptions bundle maintenance, on-site repairs, bike swaps, GPS tracking, theft protection, and remote motor control across 100+ cities in Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Belgium, Poland, Italy, and the UK. CYCLE was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; the provider publishes a consumer/business marketing and operations site but exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Euler Motors
providers.description: Euler Motors is an Indian electric commercial vehicle manufacturer headquartered in New Delhi, building battery-electric cargo and light commercial vehicles for last-mile logistics — the HiLoad and Turbo electric three-wheelers and the Storm EV four-wheeler light commercial vehicle range. Alongside the vehicles the company operates Euler Shepherd, a connected-vehicle telematics platform delivered as two end-user products: Shepherd Lite (a mobile app for real-time vehicle location, battery state of charge, range, charging status and alerts) and Shepherd Enterprise (a browser-based fleet console with trip, utilization and operations reporting). Euler Motors publishes no public developer program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, webhook catalog or partner integration documentation on any host it controls. The Shepherd web console is a single-page application whose backend answers anonymous requests with 403, so the telematics data surface is reachable only to vehicle owners inside the product. The company does publish an llms.txt at its web root, directing AI crawlers to its product, service-network and blog pages.

providers.name: Fetch Robotics
providers.description: Fetch Robotics is a provider of autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) for the manufacturing, distribution, and fulfillment industries, enabling customers to optimize warehouse and material-handling workflows through robotic automation. Its Fetch and Freight robots are programmed through a ROS (Robot Operating System) interface — standard ROS topics, services, and actions conforming to ROS Enhancement Proposals (REPs) — rather than an HTTP/REST API, and the first-party client, driver, and simulation libraries are published as open source in the fetchrobotics GitHub organization. Fetch Robotics was acquired by Zebra Technologies in August 2021 for approximately $290M; fetchrobotics.com now redirects to Zebra and the autonomous-mobile-robot product line is being wound down (2025-2026), though the open-source ROS packages remain available.

providers.name: Hopstack
providers.description: Hopstack is an AI-native, cloud-based warehouse management system (WMS) and fulfillment operations platform that helps warehouses, 3PLs, and e-commerce operators optimize inbound logistics, inventory, order processing, picking, packing, shipping, and returns across channels. Hopstack exposes a documented RESTful API (referenced at apidocs.hopstack.io) for programmatic access to core resources such as orders and consignments, secured with a per-user X-API-Key generated from the Hopstack Dashboard. API access is gated - a customer must contact Hopstack Support to enable API-key generation in the UI - and the full endpoint surface, base URL, and machine-readable specification are published behind that account/partner reference rather than as a fully open catalog.

providers.name: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: KokkanLogis Co.,Ltd. (주식회사 곳간, branded KOKKAN / 도심창고 곳간) is a South Korean urban self-storage and logistics operator headquartered in Gangnam-gu, Seoul. It rents managed storage units in five sizes (S, M, L, XL, XXL, from 1.0m cubes up to 2.0 x 2.0 x 2.0m) across 22 branches in Seoul, Busan, Incheon, Gyeonggi and Chungbuk, serving households storing seasonal appliances, clothing, bedding and baby goods as well as businesses storing samples, inventory, documents and office equipment. Customers select a branch, choose a unit size, pay and manage their contract through the KOKKAN mobile apps for iOS and Android, with recurring monthly card billing through a Korean payment gateway, long-term and promotional discounting, an address-rental (주소지 임대) product, and an optional pickup service for moving stored goods. The company also runs a franchise and partnership program for operators who want to open a KOKKAN branch. It was surfaced through the 500 Global portfolio. As of this profile KokkanLogis publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK or technical documentation — the product surface is a consumer website plus native mobile apps.

providers.name: Relay Payments
providers.description: Relay Payments operates a secure digital payment network purpose-built for the freight and trucking industry. Its mobile app and platform let carriers, owner-operators, brokers, and merchants transact contactlessly for diesel fuel, lumper (dock unloading) fees, scales, parking, truck repairs, and freight payments between brokers and carriers, replacing cash, fleet checks, and legacy fuel cards while reducing fraud and streamlining back-office reconciliation. Relay is backed by Ribbit Capital. Partner/system integration is offered under a Relay System Integration Agreement, with developer documentation gated behind partner authentication at docs.relaypayments.com; no public API specification is currently published.

providers.name: Revlon
providers.description: Revlon is a global beauty company whose portfolio spans color cosmetics, fragrance, skin care, hair color, hair care, beauty tools, and antiperspirants / deodorants. The company markets Revlon, Elizabeth Arden, Almay, Mitchum, Cutex, Charlie, SinfulColors, and Ultima II, along with a portfolio of licensed prestige and celebrity fragrance brands. Revlon Consumer Products Corporation filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the Southern District of New York on June 15, 2022 and emerged on May 2, 2023 as a privately held company controlled by its former lenders (including BrandCo noteholders such as King Street Capital, Glendon Capital, and Angelo Gordon), having cut roughly $2.7 billion of debt from its balance sheet. Today Revlon operates as a private company with reduced leverage, selling through mass-market retail and prestige channels worldwide. Revlon does not publish a public developer API; supplier, retailer, and partner integrations occur through private commercial channels (e-commerce platform integrations, EDI / GDSN feeds for retailers, and the corporate procurement portal).

providers.name: SupplyShift
providers.description: Sphera, the brand that includes the former SupplyShift, provides a Supplier Engagement solution that enables organizations to automate outreach, collect and validate supplier information, and integrate the data into risk and sustainability platforms. The software is aimed at buyers and supply chain teams seeking to improve visibility, compliance and risk scoring across their supplier base.

providers.name: 4R Systems
providers.description: 4R (4R Systems, Inc.) is a Berwyn, Pennsylvania software company founded in 1999 that sells a cloud-based intelligent inventory optimization platform and planning service to retail chains. Its prescriptive-analytics products cover demand planning, replenishment planning, allocation planning, assortment optimization, markdown optimization and vendor order optimization, combining statistical and machine-learning forecasting with a managed "planning as a service" team. Customers reach the platform through a hosted web portal and scheduled data exchanges rather than a public developer API; 4R publishes no developer portal, documentation or machine-readable API contract on its public site.

providers.name: Advantive
providers.description: Advantive is an AI-enabled software company for specialty manufacturing and distribution operations, unifying ERP, MES, quality (SPC/SQC), PLM, WMS, and B2B commerce workflows into industry-specific systems. Built from a portfolio of brands including Advantzware, DDI System, Distribution One, InfinityQS (Enact and ProFicient), Kiwiplan, WinSPC, and VIA, Advantive serves more than 2,500 customers across eight countries in verticals such as food and beverage, packaging (corrugated, folding carton, plastics), automotive, aerospace and defense, electronics, and distribution of fasteners, bearings, HVAC, and janitorial supplies. The company is a private-equity-backed operations software provider; this API Evangelist profile tracks its public digital surface. No public developer API or OpenAPI has been found — integration is delivered through the products' own connectors and the Advantive support portal.
